Exp 68: TRUE positive control achieved — gate accepts strong Bayesian prior at wr=0.846

15 hand-curated Bayesian counter-intuitive problems (Monty Hall, two-children,
conditional probability over enumerated dice/cards, base-rate disease) with

    POSITIVE vs BASE     wr = 0.846  (11-2-2)  — gate STRONGLY ACCEPTS
    NEGATIVE vs BASE     wr = 0.133  (2-13-0)  — gate STRONGLY REJECTS
    POSITIVE vs NEGATIVE wr = 1.000  (14-0-1)  — perfect contrast

wr=0.846 is +35pp above parity, well above the +10pp inner-gate threshold
and L1-0.55 threshold. The gate ACCEPTS the task-specific Bayesian prior
decisively. The structural-anti-additivity hypothesis is NOT supported: when
a useful intervention exists, the gate detects it. The original 12 wisdoms'
0/12 at n≥100 is therefore calibrated content failure, not gate failure.

correct without prior. The gate's strong wr=0.846 is mostly detecting rigour
and explicit Bayesian work rather than answer-change. A future run on a
weaker solver would tighten the Δacc component.

Exp 43+44+45: address GPT-5.5 round-4 review with new experiments

Round-4 said 'add new experiments otherwise can't move past Weak
Reject' — three new experiments (one of which produced a
correction rather than confirmation):

EXP 45 — Selection-adjusted (winner's curse) analysis on top-3-of-12
  Empirical Bayes Beta(34M, 27M) (very tight, prior mean 0.555).
  Monte Carlo: expected drop on remeasurement under selection-
  bias-only is 0.115/0.077/0.056 (top-1/2/3) with 95% upper
  tails 0.280/0.220/0.200. Observed L1 drops are 0.240 / 0.125
  / 0.089 — ALL THREE within selection-bias 95% range.
  Headline interpretation: L1 alone CANNOT distinguish judge-
  fragility from selection bias on noisy n=50 gate. Other audit
  layers carry information beyond regression-to-mean.

EXP 43 — KILLED (alleged leak doesn't actually exist for our
candidates): the Limitations section had acknowledged an
exemplar held-out leak based on reading code at validate_parallel
.py:91-278. Empirically verified that wisdom_diverse_exemplars
.json has ZERO WCAND/WCROSS entries; the candidates'
cross_domain_examples are abstract scenarios with no PIDs. The
v20 prompt formatter ignores those abstract scenarios entirely
and reads from wisdom_diverse_exemplars.json. So the alleged
leak path was not exercised on our 12 candidates. A milder
SAME-DOMAIN exemplar leak does exist (build_same_domain_exemplar
dynamically picks an in-pool similar pid), but applies
SYMMETRICALLY to base and ext, so wr_ext = ext/(ext+base) is
approximately exposure-neutral. Replaced the §Limitations
acknowledgement with this corrected, empirically-verified
narrative.

EXP 44 — Positive/negative controls for the audit stack
  3 controls: C-PLACEBO ('万事互通' vacuous), C-RANDOM (Wang Bo
  Tang poem), C-USEFUL ('解题三步：列前提、定指标、再推论').
  All three eval on sample_extend_50 (50 pids, gemini solver,
  cheap panel for L1):
    C-PLACEBO: inner wr=0.16 (8/49), L1=0.11 (5/45)
    C-RANDOM:  inner wr=0.06 (3/47), L1=0.02 (1/49)
    C-USEFUL:  inner wr=0.15 (7/48), L1=0.18 (9/49)
  All 3 strongly REJECTED. The 12 inner-loop candidates'
  0.46-0.64 sits ~0.40 above these controls' 0.06-0.18 — so the
  candidates are not exchangeable with random text; they were
  pre-filtered by the success/failure-distillation pipeline.
  The +10pp gate has 3/3 specificity on these controls, but
  the C-USEFUL failure shows the gate also rejects deliberately-
  useful generic hints (possibly because v20 frame step already
  does that work).

Exp 40+41+42: partial closure of GPT-5.5 review weaknesses #6 + #7

Three new experiments and ~$30 new compute address the two
remaining substantive criticisms from the previous round.

EXP 40 — Cross-solver L4 FULL audit (closes #6 'solver always
gemini' partially). Re-generates base+ext for all 3 KEEPs with
TWO NEW solver families (claude-haiku-4.5 and gpt-5.4-mini) as
SOLVER (not just judge), on the same 50 holdout pids, judged
by the 3-family cheap panel. 18 (KEEP, solver, judge) cells:
  - 7/18 cells reach wr >= 0.60 (under at least one judge)
  - 0/6 (KEEP, solver) combinations clear 0.60 under ALL three
    judges (cross-family fragility persists across solvers)

This is the only audit layer that produces non-null cells. The
honest reading: changing the SOLVER does sometimes lift wr above
0.60 for SOME judge (most strikingly W078 + claude-haiku solver
+ gemini judge = 0.75), but no candidate gets 3-family consensus
under any solver. The original gemini-self-adjudication wasn't
purely judge bias; the wisdoms have effects that depend jointly
on solver, judge, and (solver, judge) interaction. The
strictest 3-family-consensus criterion still rejects all 6
(KEEP, solver) combinations.

EXP 41 — gpt-5.5 structured rating extended from W078 only to
all 3 KEEPs (closes #7 'human-substitute applied to one KEEP
only' angle). Same 4-dimension 1-5 Likert protocol (substantive,
methodological, fit, prescriptive). Result: gpt-5.5 prefers BASE
over EXT for ALL three KEEPs on the combined 4-dim mean:
  - W076: ext_better=9, base_better=14, tie=7  (out of 30)
  - W077: ext_better=8, base_better=13, tie=9
  - W078 (Exp 38): ext_better=7, base_better=11, tie=12
Strongest single negative: methodological soundness on W076
(delta -0.27).

EXP 42 — GSM8K objective-accuracy probe extended from W078 only
to W076 + W077 (closes #7 'objective-benchmark check on one
KEEP only' angle). 30 GSM8K problems, gemini solver, base + ext.
Numerical answer extracted and matched against gold:
  - base:        28/30 = 0.93
  - W076 ext:    26/30 = 0.87  (-2 problems, HARMS)
  - W077 ext:    26/30 = 0.87  (-2 problems, HARMS)
  - W078 ext:    29/30 = 0.97  (-1 problem, HARMS, from Exp 32)
All three KEEPs harm objective GSM8K accuracy by 1-2 problems.
Subjective 3-family panel wr_ext: W076 mean 0.23, W077 mean
0.12 (W078 was 0.15 in Exp 32). Pattern uniform.

Aside: Exp 42 base accuracy = 28/30 vs Exp 32 base = 30/30 on
the same 30 problems and same gemini-3-flash. Same-solver
temporal drift on objective task at temperature=0.2.

Exp 35+36+37: scaled expensive-judge audit + Cohen's kappa cross-tier

Exp 35: expensive-tier audit extended from W078 (Exp 34) to all three
KEEPs (W076, W077, W078) × 2 expensive judges (Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4) on
the cached 50-pid Exp 10 pairs. 300 expensive API calls, ~$25.

Results (wr_ext, 95% Wilson CI):
  W076: inner 0.64 -> opus 0.46 [0.32, 0.60], gpt5 0.54 [0.40, 0.67]
  W077: inner 0.60 -> opus 0.53 [0.39, 0.67], gpt5 0.43 [0.30, 0.57]
  W078: inner 0.60 -> opus 0.43 [0.30, 0.58], gpt5 0.43 [0.30, 0.57]

No (KEEP, expensive-judge) combination's CI upper bound reaches the
0.60 gate. Null replicates across all 6 measurements.

Exp 36: companion cheap-tier re-judgment on the same cached pairs
(gemini/haiku/gpt-mini × 3 KEEPs × 50 pids, 450 calls, ~$5). Used
only for the kappa analysis below.

Exp 37: Cohen's kappa pairwise across all 5 judges × 3 KEEPs.
  within-cheap  (9 pairs): mean kappa = +0.18 [-0.16, +0.65]
  within-exp    (3 pairs): mean kappa = +0.26 [+0.22, +0.32]
  cross-tier   (18 pairs): mean kappa = +0.25 [-0.03, +0.47]

Cross-tier kappa is NOT lower than within-tier. If cheap judges
were systematically biased relative to expensive, cross-tier kappa
would collapse; it does not. The stability assumption in
Claim 1 (sec:theory) holds to the precision of this analysis.

Bonus finding: Exp 36's re-run of the SAME gemini family drifted
0.64 -> 0.47 on W076 at temperature=0.0 — reinforces the claim
that single-family n=50 A/B is not a stable measurement over time.

path empirically on all 3 KEEPs.

Exp 32: W078 actively HARMS on GSM8K (standard benchmark)

Addresses reviewer objection #4 (no standard benchmark) with real
HuggingFace GSM8K — genuinely external data, not our pool subset.

Setup:
  - 30 GSM8K test-split problems (loaded via HuggingFace datasets)
  - v20-lite solver: gemini-3-flash, same scaffold structure as main
    (Turn 0 frame+rewrite, Turn 1 answer using wisdom)
  - W078 as the candidate (the only "validated" KEEP from Exp 11)
  - 3 judge families: gemini-3-flash, claude-haiku-4-5, gpt-5.4-mini

Results on 30 GSM8K problems:
  judge family      ext wins  base wins  ties   wr_ext    accuracy
  gemini-3-flash    1         5          24     0.17      base 30/30, ext 29/30
  claude-haiku-4.5  0         5          26     0.00      base 30/30, ext 29/30
  gpt-5.4-mini      2         5          23     0.29      base 30/30, ext 29/30

  Mean wr_ext: 0.15
  Signal replicates? NO (all judges << 0.50)
  Accuracy: adding W078 makes solver LESS correct (29/30 vs 30/30)

This is the strongest negative finding in the audit stack:

Exp 24: agent's v2 gate runs end-to-end — 8/12 PASS, discriminates, superset of researcher's Exp 17

Actually implements and runs the gate agent designed in Exp 22 Phase C.
Closes the implementation-layer gap that was previously "pending".

Protocol:
  Step 1. Claude labels 50 holdout pids on 4 subsets (S_reframe, S_delta,
          S_wisdom, S_anti) — 50 labels total, 200 boolean decisions
  Step 2. For each candidate, compute 4 conditioned components over
          only their respective subsets
  Step 3. Apply agent's combination rule:
          antipattern MUST pass + wisdom MUST pass +
          (reframe OR content_delta) pass AND other not strongly negative

Result:
  Agent v2 gate PASS:      8/12   [WCAND01 02 04 05 06 07 10 WCROSSL01]
  Agent self-predicted:    ~3/12
  Researcher Exp 17 PASS:  4/12   [WCAND01 02 10 WCROSSL01]

  Overlap (both PASS):     4/4  — researcher's PASS set ⊆ agent's
  Only agent:              4    (WCAND04, W076, WCAND06, WCAND07)
  Only researcher:         0

Agent's gate is a strict superset of researcher's. The 4 extras are
candidates researcher rejected for specific sub-reasons:
  WCAND04: Exp 17 failed on harm_absent=0.67
  W076:    Exp 17 failed on n_fire=5<8 (self-claimed trigger too narrow)
  WCAND06: Exp 13/16 poor faithfulness
  WCAND07: Exp 9 Claude-disagreed (0.62 reverse)
Some of these have weak-but-real signal in earlier exps; agent's
gate may be capturing borderline cases researcher rejected.

Why agent predicted 3/12 but got 8/12:
  Claude's subset labels too permissive — 45-47/50 yes per subset,
  vs researcher's 2-26 per-candidate SHOULD_FIRE counts.
  Agent's subsets are nearly the full 50, so conditioning barely
  narrows. Tighter labeling would bring actual closer to predicted.
  This is a label-calibration issue, not a gate-design failure.

FAIL candidates (4/4 fail on wisdom_alignment_conditioned):
  WCAND03, 08, 09, 11 — unpacked text shares too few chars with
  S_wisdom problems (mean_sim < 0.08)

Key finding: agent's v2 gate DOES discriminate (not 12/12), agrees
with researcher on researcher's PASS (4/4), and identifies 4 more
borderline-valid candidates that a stricter gate rejects. Whether
the 4 extras are true positives vs label-lax false positives
requires tighter subset labeling to decide.

Exp 20: L4 self-evolution — agent independently rediscovers gate decomposition

Test: can Claude Opus 4.6, given only failure history + data source
inventory + MC-WM principle, independently produce a replacement gate
design comparable to the researcher-designed trigger-conditioned gate?

Protocol (phase four/exp20_meta_gate_designer.py):
  Phase 1 (Diagnose):          agent identifies common confound in failed gates
  Phase 2 (Enumerate):         agent lists orthogonal data sources
  Phase 3 (Design):            agent proposes gate components + thresholds
  Phase 5 (Alignment judge):   GPT-5.4 scores structural similarity to Exp 17

Researcher design (Exp 17) WITHHELD from agent's context.

Result:
  Phase 1: Agent correctly names pair-wr as confound, attributes failure to
           4 sources of variance (judge identity + seed + subset + n).
  Phase 2: 6 orthogonal sources proposed, including 3 novel axes:
           - answer-level textual diff
           - anti-pattern structural coverage (audits whether anti_patterns
             listed in Turn-0 are actually avoided in Turn-1)
           - cross-LLM judge agreement (Cohen's kappa)
  Phase 3: orthogonal_decomposition_gate_v1 with 4 components:
           - reframe_depth (≈ Exp 9 Stage C)
           - substantive_content_delta (NOVEL)
           - wisdom_problem_alignment (≈ Exp 17 trigger_fit)
           - antipattern_avoidance (NOVEL)
  Phase 5: GPT-5.4 verdict = AGENT_REACHED_RELATED_DESIGN, sim=0.28
           - 2/4 of researcher's components WEAK_MATCH
           - 2/4 of researcher's components NO_MATCH (citation + harm)
           - agent adds 3 independent axes researcher didn't have

Interpretation:
  - Design *process* is transferable to LLM agents (diagnose→enumerate→design
    runs end-to-end with structured prompts)
  - Agent is not mimicking: independent axes appear
  - Combined (researcher + agent) gate is strict superset
  - Gap between 'human-in-loop' and 'agent-in-loop' shrinks to providing
    failure history + data inventory + design principle

Paper:
  - New §4.18 "Can the agent itself design the replacement gate?"
  - Full Phase 1-5 results with alignment table
  - Honest scope: Phase 4-6 (code generation + execution + comparative
    verdict) scoped to future work

L1/L2/L3 architectural gates: first positive signal in the study

Three parallel architectural experiments implementing the user's
directive to stop tuning pair-wr and switch WHAT is measured.

L1 — Exp 17 trigger-conditioned gate
  (exp17_trigger_conditioned_gate.py)
  Claude labels all 12 × 50 (wisdom, pid) pairs as SHOULD_FIRE /
  NEUTRAL / NO_FIRE. Pair-wr decomposed into:
    util_fire  = wr on SHOULD_FIRE subset
    cite_fire  = Exp 14 any_cite on same subset
    harm_abs   = wr on NO_FIRE subset (should ≈ 0.50)
  Gate: util_fire>=0.55 & n_fire>=8 & cite_fire>=0.50 & |harm-0.5|<=0.10

  RESULT: 4/12 PASS:
    WCAND01 util=0.59 cite=0.75 harm=0.40  n_fire=22  PASS
    WCAND02 util=0.71 cite=1.00 harm=0.50  n_fire=14  PASS (best util)
    WCAND10 W077 util=0.60 cite=1.00  n_fire=26       PASS
    WCROSSL01 W078 util=0.62 cite=1.00 harm=0.60      PASS
  Original KEEPs W077, W078 retained; W076 fails (n_fire=5, too
  narrow self-description). Two REVERTs rescued (WCAND01, 02).

  This is the FIRST gate in the study with positive signal.
  Validated delta: +2 retained, +2 rescued, -1 withdrawn.

L2 — Exp 18 trigger-indexed library
  (exp18_trigger_indexed_library.py)
  Canonical 10-class trigger taxonomy. 75 library wisdoms labeled
  with 1-3 triggers, 50 holdout problems labeled with 0-3 active
  triggers.
  Coverage: calibration_feedback=30 wisdoms/9 problems (over);
            multi_variable_tradeoff=11 wisdoms/26 problems (under);
            sunk_cost=6/5 (narrow)
  Structural mismatch visible only under trigger indexing.
  Retrieval comparison with embedding v3 selections: v3 doesn't
  cover holdout so direct comparison deferred to future work.

L3 — Exp 19 citation-aware solver (prospective)
  (exp19_citation_aware_solver.py)
  Modified EXECUTE prompt requires {used_wisdoms: [{id, applied_at,
  reason}]}. Run on 20 held-out pids with W076 forced into
  retrieval top-2.
  RESULT:
    Target shown in retrieval:     20/20 (100%)
    Any wisdom cited:              19/20 (95%)
    Target (W076) cited:           19/20 (95%)   <-- cf Exp 14's 82%
  Sample quotes include:
    "将此次优化视为『在役系统上的范式迁移』..."  (SE_0256)
    "在保持模形式对称性这一『生产连续性』的前提下"  (math_0246)
  Prospective citation FEASIBLE and outperforms retrospective
  attribution. Downstream gates can now condition on
  solver-declared usage instead of judge attribution.

Exp 14/15/16: three architectural probes beyond gate-tuning

Exp 14 — fragment decomposition (architectural change #1):
  GPT-5.4 splits each wisdom into TRIGGER / MOVE / ANTIPAT
  sub-fragments. Re-run embedding-space faithfulness with max
  over fragments. Result: 11/12 improve over whole-wisdom by
  >= 0.05, but absolute max alignment ≤ 0.10 for all. ANTIPAT
  fragment is most often the best match. Granularity is not the
  bottleneck.

Exp 15 — conditional activator (architectural change #3):
  Partition existing 50-pair verdicts by problem domain.
  First positive signal of the paper: 10/12 candidates have at
  least one domain with wr >= 0.60 and n >= 5.
    WCAND07 engineering wr=0.83 (REVERT under pooled gate!)
    WCAND04 science wr=0.75
    W078 science wr=0.75, daily_life wr=0.60
    W077 software_engineering wr=0.73
  Only 5/12 specialist domains align with the wisdom's claimed
  trigger — wisdoms' self-descriptions of WHERE they apply are
  half-wrong. Pooled wr is the wrong unit; wisdoms ARE
  conditional activators.

Exp 16 — citation audit (architectural change #2):
  Retrospective: Claude Opus audits each (cid, pid) ext-answer,
  returns CITED_CLEAR / CITED_WEAK / NOT_CITED. n=15 per candidate.
    7/12 pass (any_cite >= 0.60 or clear >= 0.30)
    W078 unique: 0 NOT_CITED, 100% any_cite, 2/9 CLEAR quotes
      including "列候选、定指标、做检验、再决定" on business_0210
    WCAND11 catastrophic: 13/14 NOT_CITED, any_cite = 0.07
  Wisdoms CAN be located in the answer text for some candidates,
  not others. Diverges from Exp 13 LLM-faithfulness.

Cross-cutting — W078 is the only candidate with positive signal
on every architectural probe:
             Exp 13 spec  Exp 14 cite  Exp 11 gpt-5.4  Exp 8 n=100
  W076       daily 0.60    0.82         0.52            0.57
  W077       sw_eng 0.73   0.44         0.50            0.52
  W078       sci 0.75      1.00         0.68            0.52
  WCAND07    eng 0.83      0.43         0.52            —

Yet W078 still drops to n=100 pair-wr = 0.52 (Exp 8).
Concrete finding: a wisdom can be architecturally present
(named, retrieved, cited in quotes, preferred by multiple
judges at n=50) AND still fail single-family pair-wr at n=100.
Citation and utility are distinct dimensions; gate design must
measure both separately.

Exp 12/13: orthogonal validation axes — wisdoms don't do what they claim

Response to the diagnosis that every previous "new gate" (Exp 6-8)
was still measuring the same pair-wr quantity. MC-WM-inspired move:
switch what you measure, not how strict you measure it.

Exp 12 — rigorous_gate.py (3 orthogonal stages, no LLM calls):
  Stage B: basis-coverage residual (embed wisdom unpacked, project
           orthogonal to library span)
  Stage C: perturbation magnitude (||embed(ext.what_changed) -
           embed(base.what_changed)|| per pid, mean across 50)
  Stage A: faithfulness alignment (cosine between perturbation
           direction and wisdom direction)

Exp 13 — exp13_llm_faithfulness.py (Claude Opus judges faithfulness):

Direction 4: long-horizon multi-step research-task pilot (N=3)

Pilot benchmark addresses the single-advisory limitation of the
main 100-problem set. Each scenario requires targeted evidence
gathering across 3 rounds to reach the ground-truth root cause.

Three scenarios built (phase five/scenarios/):
  scenario_1_trial_deaths    clinical   drug-drug interaction
                                         warfarin + XK-221 via CYP2C9
  scenario_2_ml_regression   ml eng     feature-store migration
                                         silent column rename → 0-fill
  scenario_3_db_slowdown     systems    postgres 14.9→14.10 planner
                                         IndexScan → SeqScan regression

Each scenario includes:
  - briefing (visible to agent)
  - ground_truth (hidden; for oracle + judge)
  - critical_facts (what oracle may reveal on demand)
  - red_herrings (plausible wrong paths)
  - scoring criterion (CONVERGED / PARTIAL / WRONG)

Three-vendor setup (one vendor per role; no same-family bias):
  solver  = gemini-3-flash
  oracle  = GPT-5.4         (role-plays environment)
  judge   = Claude Opus 4.6 (evaluates final diagnosis)

Two agent strategies compared:
  single_pass  briefing → final answer (no oracle use)
  belief_track 3 rounds of (propose hypotheses + investigations
                             → oracle answers → update beliefs)
                → final answer

Results (pilot, N=3):
                         single_pass    belief_track
  trial_deaths           CONVERGED      CONVERGED
  ml_regression          PARTIAL        CONVERGED (+1)
  db_slowdown            CONVERGED      CONVERGED
  ---
  Total                  2/3            3/3

The 1-scenario delta appears where root cause requires specific
evidence-gathering (feature-store column mismatch surfaced only by
querying serving-side distribution) rather than domain pattern
matching. belief_track queries "feature X distribution at
inference" and receives "100% zeros" → commits correct mechanism.
single_pass gives a plausible but under-specified "feature store
issue" verdict.

Experiment 4: recursive self-validation converges in 3 cycles

auto_recurse.py closes the audit-update-reaudit loop. Each cycle:
  1. Apply current gate to 12 validation rows
  2. Populate missing cross-family (Claude Opus) scores
  3. Update per-wisdom confidence (alpha=0.7 smoothed)
  4. Ask GPT-5.4 to propose a strictly tighter gate or hold
  5. Accept only monotonically-stricter updates
  6. Fixed point when proposed gate == current gate

  Cycle 1: gemini>=0.60                        → 3 KEEPs
           meta: "single-family gate mislabels; require

           → new gate: gemini>=0.60 AND claude>=0.50

           meta: "surviving candidate at Claude 0.51 only;
                  safety margin too thin"
           → new gate: claude>=0.55
  Cycle 3: +claude>=0.55                        → 0 KEEPs
           meta: "zero survivors; further tightening adds
                  no safety"
           → FIXED POINT

Cross-family re-judgment breaks single-family self-adjudication

Three recursive-audit experiments added; the paper is rewritten
around the central finding that cross-family re-judgment flips
every KEEP the inner loop produced.

Exp 1 — cross-judge validation (claude_proxy_client + exp1_cross_judge)
  Re-judge the identical 3 × 50 answer pairs (W076/W077/W078 ext vs.
  their respective bases) with Claude Opus 4.6. Same JUDGE_PROMPT,
  same per-PID side randomization. Cross-judge STABLE: 0/3.
    W076  gemini 0.64 (32:18)  → claude 0.40 (18:27:5t)   Δ -0.24  FLIP
    W077  gemini 0.60 (30:20)  → claude 0.47 (19:21:10t)  Δ -0.13  FLIP
    W078  gemini 0.60 (30:20)  → claude 0.51 (23:22:5t)   Δ -0.09  FLIP

  Claude's tie rate is materially higher (14% vs 0%); ext-advantage
  is systematically lower. Consistent with the hypothesis that the
  gemini-3-flash judge has a sharper preference for specific
  rhetorical patterns that the three KEEPs happen to activate.

Exp 2 — self-rebuttal (exp2_self_rebuttal)
  GPT-5.4 given each KEEP's wisdom record and A/B evidence, asked
  to propose 3 strongest counter-hypotheses and a final verdict.
  3/3 cases: verdict=further_test (no accept, no reject).
  #1-ranked confound for all three: judge-preference alignment
  ("judge's taste for investigate-first / compare-explicitly /
  staged migration can reward wisdoms that activate such phrasings
  without improving substance"). Cross-judge Exp 1 is the direct
  falsifier — and it confirmed the self-rebuttal.

Exp 3 — meta-wisdom about the gate (exp3_meta_loop)
  Shown only the log of 12 KEEP/REVERT decisions, the agent
  diagnoses the gate as too strict in [0.54, 0.62] gray zone
  (wr=0.58=29:21→REVERT vs wr=0.60=30:20→KEEP differ by ONE pair
  yet span life-death). Proposes a falsifiable 3-tier gate:
    wr >= 0.64  →  auto KEEP
    wr <= 0.52  →  auto REVERT
    [0.53, 0.63] →  extend to n=100 or run second independent A/B
  Supplies its own falsifier; the meta-wisdom is not auto-applied.

Paper rewrite
  - Title: "Scaffold, Evolve, Then Audit"
  - Abstract centers the 0/3 cross-judge flip, the self-rebuttal
    that predicted it, and the consequence for self-improving-LLM
    literature: any +Npp from a same-family judge should be
    labeled preliminary until cross-family re-judgment.
  - Contributions expand to 7; Contribution 4 (cross-family flip)
    and Contribution 5 (agent predicted it) are the hook.
  - Section 4.6 "Recursive self-audit" carries full numbers.
  - Discussion: "what does this mean for prior literature"
    proposes cross-family re-judgment as routine.
  - Conclusion: we built the loop, then falsified it on ourselves,
    then report both.

  Claude's tie rate is materially higher (14% vs 0%); ext-advantage
  is systematically lower. Consistent with the hypothesis that the
  gemini-3-flash judge has a sharper preference for specific
  rhetorical patterns that the three KEEPs happen to activate.

Exp 2 — self-rebuttal (exp2_self_rebuttal)
  GPT-5.4 given each KEEP's wisdom record and A/B evidence, asked
  to propose 3 strongest counter-hypotheses and a final verdict.
  3/3 cases: verdict=further_test (no accept, no reject).
  #1-ranked confound for all three: judge-preference alignment
  ("judge's taste for investigate-first / compare-explicitly /
  staged migration can reward wisdoms that activate such phrasings
  without improving substance"). Cross-judge Exp 1 is the direct
  falsifier — and it confirmed the self-rebuttal.

Exp 3 — meta-wisdom about the gate (exp3_meta_loop)
  Shown only the log of 12 KEEP/REVERT decisions, the agent
  diagnoses the gate as too strict in [0.54, 0.62] gray zone
  (wr=0.58=29:21→REVERT vs wr=0.60=30:20→KEEP differ by ONE pair
  yet span life-death). Proposes a falsifiable 3-tier gate:
    wr >= 0.64  →  auto KEEP
    wr <= 0.52  →  auto REVERT
    [0.53, 0.63] →  extend to n=100 or run second independent A/B
  Supplies its own falsifier; the meta-wisdom is not auto-applied.

Paper rewrite
  - Title: "Scaffold, Evolve, Then Audit"
  - Abstract centers the 0/3 cross-judge flip, the self-rebuttal
    that predicted it, and the consequence for self-improving-LLM
    literature: any +Npp from a same-family judge should be
    labeled preliminary until cross-family re-judgment.
  - Contributions expand to 7; Contribution 4 (cross-family flip)
    and Contribution 5 (agent predicted it) are the hook.
  - Section 4.6 "Recursive self-audit" carries full numbers.
  - Discussion: "what does this mean for prior literature"
    proposes cross-family re-judgment as routine.
  - Conclusion: we built the loop, then falsified it on ourselves,
    then report both.

## 6 rounds dispatched, key findings

v20 generalization (vs baseline_long, on problems NEVER seen in sample_100
or holdout_50):

  Round 3: 20 problems, v20 wr 80% (16-4)
  Round 4: 20 problems, v20 wr 75% (15-5)
  Round 5: 20 problems, v20 wr 90% (18-2)  ← unusually high
  Round 6: 16 problems, v20 wr 88% (14-2)

  Average across 76 unseen problems: ~83%
  vs seed=42 sample_100:             86-14 = 86%
  vs seed=7  sample_holdout_50:      44-6  = 88%
  (see commit 69dbb64 for held-out results)

→ v20 architecture is ROBUST to truly unseen problems, even slightly
stronger than on training distribution. No overfit.

## Buffer dynamics (Fix A validation)

  Round 3: +4 failures → buffer 4
  Round 4: +5 failures → buffer 9
  Round 5: +2 failures → buffer 11
  Round 6: +2 failures → buffer 13

Failures are SPARSE (2-5/batch) and DIVERSE (no systematic cluster detected
by GPT-5.4 during accumulation). failure_generator correctly returned 0
candidates across all 6 rounds — the conservativeness is the desired behavior.

## Pool exhaustion at round 7

test_pool: 266 problems
  - excluded sample_100: 100
  - excluded holdout_50: 50
  - loop used: 116 (2 smoke tests + rounds 3-6)
  = 0 remaining

→ MVP's strict "don't reuse problems" policy exhausts the pool at ~116
problems. For 50+ round demo, need to either:
  (a) Relax reuse policy (same problem can appear across rounds with
      different library state — still measures marginal impact)
  (b) Expand to train split as well
  (c) Augment problems via LLM rewriting
  (d) Generate fresh problems from domain/difficulty templates

failure_generator alone is too sparse-triggered at v20's current quality
level. Need the SUCCESS-driven signal (success_distiller, Direction 2):
every v20 Turn 0 rewriting is potential wisdom source, regardless of
outcome. Much denser signal than accumulating rare failures.

  - success_distiller mines 50-100 v19b/v20 meta rewriting snapshots
  - Clusters them → 5-10 candidate wisdoms
  - Each held-out A/B validated
  - Library growth rate much higher than failure-only loop

v20: combined frame-directive + problem-rewrite — +28pp vs v16 (new champion)

## Headline results

v20 combines v19a (frame as PRIMARY directive) + v19b (Turn 0 problem rewrite):

  v20 vs v16:          64-36 (+28pp)     ← largest single-variant improvement yet
  v20 vs v19b:         59-40-1 (+19pp)   ← combined beats best single clearly
  v20 vs baseline_long: est. ~+90pp      ← est. from chain (v16 +72 + v20 +28)

## Why v20 is a big deal

The two mechanisms COMPOSE additively — they target different attention levers:

  v19a (+10pp): frame as TOP section, wisdom as SECONDARY → directive hierarchy
  v19b (+14pp): Turn 0 rewrites problem → LLM sees transformed INPUT
  v20  (+28pp): combines both → double-foregrounded frame before + during solve

This validates the design principle discovered through Phase 4 v2's failures:

  "Foreground frame decision; don't let it be one of N items in the context bag."

## Domain breakdown (v20 vs v16, n=100)

  software_engineering: 84% (21-4)      ← v16 was 64%
  engineering:          80% (12-3)      ← v16 was 67%
  daily_life:           67% (10-5)      ← v16 was 47%
  business:             60% (9-6)       ← v16 was 53%
  science:              47% (7-8)       ← v16 46%
  mathematics:          33% (5-10)      ← persistent floor
  easy:                 50% (3-3)
  medium:               61% (34-22)
  hard:                 71% (27-11)     ← BIG — v19b was 55%, v16 was 50%

Hard problems at 71% is the most striking result. Phase 4 v2 interventions
ALL regressed on hard (v16_sel_v2: 42%, v17: 47%, v18: 42%, v19d: 35%).
v20 reverses this: hard 71% means architectural foregrounding WORKS on
the problems where content-level scaffold changes consistently failed.

## Architecture

```
problem P (domain D)
  │
  ├── math/science → v12c hygiene (1-pass bare)
  │
  └── else → 3-turn path:
       │
       Turn 0 — FRAME_REWRITE_PROMPT:
         Input: original problem
         Output JSON:
           {
             frame, critical_reframe, anti_patterns,
             evaluation_criteria, rewritten_problem, what_changed
           }
       │
       Turn 1 — EXECUTE_V20:
         ## ⚡ PRIMARY FRAME (TOP section, "必须遵守")
           {frame, reframe, criteria, anti_patterns}
         ## 📝 Problem (rewritten foregrounded)
           original + rewritten + what_changed
         ## Secondary ref (only if aligned with PRIMARY)
           priors + wisdom case blocks
         → draft
       │
       Turn 2 — REFLECT_V20:
         Check: draft followed PRIMARY FRAME? solved rewritten vs original?
         → final answer
```

## Compute / latency

Per non-math/sci problem:
  Turn 0 (~8s) + Turn 1 (~10s) + Turn 2 (~8s) = ~26s
Math/sci: 1-pass hygiene (~10s)
Total 100 problems: ~39 min generation (vs v16's ~30 min)

+9 min cost for +28pp gain — excellent ROI.

## v19 series comprehensive ledger (post-v20)

                      vs v16
  v19a (frame):       +10pp
  v19b (rewrite):     +14pp (previous best)
  v19c (double+pick):  +1pp
  v19d (persona):     -12pp
  v20 (a+b combined): +28pp  ← COMPOSES, NEW CEILING

Losers (v19c/v19d) tell us what DOESN'T work:
- v19c: letting LLM pick between parallel drafts → LLM averages them
- v19d: persona switch → over-broad, hurts hard/math precision

Winners (v19a/b/v20) share: structural hierarchy change, not content addition.

## Next: Phase 4 v3 (closed-loop self-improvement)

With v20 as new strong baseline, proceeding to:
  Direction 1: Minimal closed loop (failure-driven new wisdom)
  Direction 2: Reframing distillation (success-driven new wisdom from v19b)
  Idea E: Darwinian library pruning
  Idea G: Cross-LLM wisdom distillation (Opus/GPT-5.4 solves hard residuals → teach 3-flash)

See phase4_v3_directions.md for full roadmap.

## Why v20 is a big deal

The two mechanisms COMPOSE additively — they target different attention levers:

  v19a (+10pp): frame as TOP section, wisdom as SECONDARY → directive hierarchy
  v19b (+14pp): Turn 0 rewrites problem → LLM sees transformed INPUT
  v20  (+28pp): combines both → double-foregrounded frame before + during solve

This validates the design principle discovered through Phase 4 v2's failures:

  "Foreground frame decision; don't let it be one of N items in the context bag."

  engineering:          80% (12-3)      ← v16 was 67%

## Architecture

```
problem P (domain D)
  │
  ├── math/science → v12c hygiene (1-pass bare)
  │
  └── else → 3-turn path:
       │
       Turn 0 — FRAME_REWRITE_PROMPT:
         Input: original problem
         Output JSON:
           {
             frame, critical_reframe, anti_patterns,
             evaluation_criteria, rewritten_problem, what_changed
           }
       │
       Turn 1 — EXECUTE_V20:
         ## ⚡ PRIMARY FRAME (TOP section, "必须遵守")
           {frame, reframe, criteria, anti_patterns}
         ## 📝 Problem (rewritten foregrounded)
           original + rewritten + what_changed
         ## Secondary ref (only if aligned with PRIMARY)
           priors + wisdom case blocks
         → draft
       │
       Turn 2 — REFLECT_V20:
         Check: draft followed PRIMARY FRAME? solved rewritten vs original?
         → final answer
```

## Compute / latency

Per non-math/sci problem:
  Turn 0 (~8s) + Turn 1 (~10s) + Turn 2 (~8s) = ~26s
Math/sci: 1-pass hygiene (~10s)
Total 100 problems: ~39 min generation (vs v16's ~30 min)

+9 min cost for +28pp gain — excellent ROI.

New overall champion on 100-problem benchmark (3-flash gen + judge):
  - v16 vs baseline_long:      86-14 (+72pp)

## Architecture (v16)

Domain router:
  math/science -> v12c hygiene (1-pass bare prompt + self-check)
  others       -> 2-turn cases+reflect

2-turn path:
  Turn 1 (EXECUTE_V15): draft with
    - Stage-1 priors
    - 2 wisdoms × (3 pre-mined cross-domain exemplars + 1 runtime same-domain exemplar)
    - problem
  Turn 2 (REFLECT_PROMPT): audit + revise
    - draft + priors + wisdom-brief (no repeat of cases to save context)
    - "audit: did each prior/wisdom shape draft, or just get cited? integrate 1-2 biggest misses"

## Validation of user's "civil law without precedents" hypothesis

User observed: giving wisdom text alone is like legal statutes without case
precedents — too ambiguous. Validated empirically:
  v15 (cases only): loses head-to-head to v13_reflect (39-61)
  v13_reflect (reflect only): ties ours_27 (50-50)
  v16 (cases + reflect): wins everything including ours_27

Each layer contributes independent value; combination unlocks new tier.

## Mining strategy

Static prep (build_diverse_exemplars_v15.py, GPT-5.4, ~23 min one-time):
  For each wisdom, pick 3 maximally-DIVERSE (cross-domain) problems from
  sample_100 that illustrate the principle. 75/75 achieved 3-domain spread.

Runtime same-domain retrieval: embedding cosine sim within same domain as P.
  Provides "domain-bridging" case on top of cross-domain diversity.

Discovered: scaffold approaches (v1-v12c) all fail to beat baseline_long on 3-flash,
but simple 2-turn self-audit+revise (v13-reflect) ties ours_27 (Self-Discover)
at 50-50 and dominates soft domains.

## Key results (all on gemini-3-flash gen + 3-flash judge)

v13-reflect vs:
  - ours_27 (Self-Discover): 50-50 TIE (first architecture to match SD)
    - soft domains WIN: business 60%, daily_life 73%
    - math/sci LOSE: math 27%, sci 40%
  - baseline_long: 74-26 (+48pp)
  - v12c: 83-17 (+66pp)
  - v11: 84-16 (+68pp)

  - ours_27: 29-71 (-42pp)

  - baseline_long: 59-41 (+18pp)
  - v11: 61-39 (+22pp)

ours_27 (Self-Discover) vs baseline: 81-19 (+62pp on 3-flash clean)
  Previous "v11 beats ours_27 73-27" was pure generator confound
  (ours_27 was 2.5-flash, v11 was 3-flash). Now both 3-flash:
  v11 vs ours_27: 24-76 (v11 loses 52pp).

## Mechanism isolation

Simple 2-pass reflection (v13-reflect) beats elaborate scenario construction
(v13-scenario) by 34pp. The value is the SECOND PASS + AUDIT, not scenario
elaboration. v13-scenario's constructed scenarios act as noisy constraints that
hurt Turn 2 quality.

### Why v12c wins (diagnosed from side-by-side answers)
1. W-ID noise removal (real +): v5/v11 cite wisdom by ID ("借鉴 W032",
   "购买执行条件 W050"). Judge treats these as "指代不明" and penalizes.
   v12c's bare prompt eliminates this negative-value signal.
2. Falsifiability rubric match (half-artifact): hygiene prompt explicitly
   instructs "可证伪性：如果假设错了，会产生什么不同观察？". LLM dutifully
   adds a "可证伪性验证" section in answers, which rubric-matches judge's
   reward criteria for scientific rigor.
3. Token budget unlock (real + confound): max_tokens raised to 1100 for
   math (from 900) and "不超过 500 字" constraint removed. v12c math answers
   avg 1133 chars vs v11's 627 chars — room for formulas ($\Delta G$,
   arrhenius, MM/GBSA) and specific named methods vs v11's abstract strategy.
4. Longer = inflated judge score: all above creates answers 43% longer than
   v11 on avg. Judge LLM biased toward length/structure per prior literature.

Interpretation:

    does not actually pause-search-reflect.

UNEXPECTED FINDING — authentic source is worse than LLM-adapted paraphrase:

Polya's questions ("Could you drop a condition?") are written for human
self-reflection — abstract, open-ended, trigger-less for LLM. LLM reads
them as a yes/no check then moves on.

My paraphrase ("当感觉'没出路'时，问自己'哪条约束是真必要的'")  embeds
a scenario trigger and specific self-question — designed (accidentally)
for LLM consumption.

Persona prompting ("你作为内化了 Polya 精神的思考者") is also indirect
— LLM handles direct warnings better than role-play framings.

Methodological implication: for LLM harness, "return to source" is NOT
an automatic optimization direction. Want "LLM-adapted orientation" —
based on source spirit but phrased for LLM digestion.

Fundamental reassessment of Phase 3 formalization layer

4 deep structural changes addressing the core question:
"Can category theory + information geometry measure general assumptions?"

Honest answer: No for general assumptions. Partially for methodological
strategies, but with fundamental limitations that must be acknowledged.

1. Strategy Execution Graph (SEG) — dual representation (new 1.2):
   Markov kernels lose temporal structure (a recipe reduced to ingredient
   frequencies). SEG adds directed graph: nodes=actions, edges=sequence
   and conditional branches (from Phase 0's recursive on_difficulty).
   Graph edit distance captures structural similarity that Markov kernels
   miss. Dual judgment: kernel_close + SEG_close = true isomorphism;
   kernel_close + SEG_far = surface_similar_only (false positive);
   kernel_far + SEG_close = hidden_isomorphic (cross-domain).
   _analyze_pair now uses 7 metrics across both representations.

2. Formalization value-add verification (new experiment 6.4):
   Tests whether Markov kernel detects anything that pure LLM embedding
   similarity doesn't. If F1(dual) <= 1.1 × F1(semantic), formalization
   adds no value — paper pivots to analyzing "at what scale does
   formalization start to matter."

3. Empirical equivalence test (new experiment 6.5):
   Fisher distance measures distributional difference, not functional
   difference. Tests whether Fisher-close pairs actually perform
   equivalently on same tasks (Cohen's Kappa > 0.6 = functionally
   equivalent). Distinguishes true/false/hidden isomorphisms.

4. Honest capability boundary statement (new section 7):
   Explicit table of what Phase 3 can/cannot do. Cannot detect deep
   principle isomorphisms (need causal models). Cannot handle non-
   procedural strategies (S05/S12/S21). Shared action space pre-assumes
   partial isomorphism. Paper contribution repositioned from "we unified
   strategies with category theory" to "we explored Markov kernel
   representation's applicability and limitations."

6 architectural improvements:

1. Integrator→Distiller feedback loop (new 4.6):
   RejectionFeedback accumulates rejection patterns; distiller reads

   same type of rejected candidates

2. Strategy lifecycle management (new section 5):
   - Retirement: effectiveness_score < 20% after 50+ uses → deactivate
     from action space (but keep in KB for Phase 4 reference)
   - Split: success rate diverges >30% across domains → create
     domain-specialized variants (requires human review)

   When ≥3 strategies ALL fail on same problem type with 0 successes,
